title: Mackinnon:
length: about 85 s (about 75 s with the optional lift)
headline: Information does not move people. Stories do. People are always worth showing up for.
story: Mackinnon answers one question: what have you learned? Honestly, she has unlearned more. Facts do not move people. Stories do.

The story is Thu Ta: strangers funded his heart surgery, and today he brings health care back to people in Myanmar. Then scale, and then the lesson: it is about people. Warm, sure, hopeful. It ends on “People are always worth showing up for.”
do: Use the second take only. Start on “I get asked a lot” in the second run.
Open on frame 1 with “What have you learned?” on top.
Spell Thu Ta in two words.
Hold 1 second after the last line.
dont: Never use the first run or “I'm gonna start over”.
No title card or logo at 0:00.
No Medellín patient B-roll as Thu Ta.
No more than one brand element on screen at a time.
No dramatic music on the war line.

bp_intro: All source times are in Mincho5161.MP4 (2:46, one 4K camera, Mackinnon only). Use the second run, from about 01:16. Times come from the transcript.json and are accurate to about 0.2 s, except the first word of the second run: find it on the waveform. Every frame is from the real file. The yellow box shows the 9:16 crop. For the 16:9 version, use the same cut with no crop.

rows.frame_alt: Mackinnon in a beige blouse, seated, dark green wall behind
rows.visual: Mackinnon, wide and locked-off. Second take only. In-point on “I” of “I get asked a lot” in the second run (about 01:15–01:16, find it on the waveform). Never use the first run (00:11–00:58).
rows.motion: Question on top from frame 1, top third: What have you learned? (her own words). Lato Bold, Watsi yellow #FFCC33, soft shadow. Cut on. Stays to 00:05.5. Captions start with her voice.

voice.quote: I get asked a lot, what have you learned? And the honest answer is I've probably unlearned more than I've learned.

rows.visual: Same shot. Keep the pause before “Stories do.” It is the point.
rows.motion: Question fades out at 00:05.5 (6 frames). Name super “Mackinnon” at 00:07–00:09, lower left, above the captions, large. First name only.

voice.quote: I used to think the gap was information, that if people just knew how many people needed health care, they'd act. I learned pretty quickly that information alone doesn't move people. Stories do.

rows.music: Music enters on “Stories do.” Warm, sustained piano or guitar bed, 18–20 dB under her voice. No drums.

rows.frame_alt: Mackinnon with both hands up, telling Thu Ta's story
rows.visual: On her. 106% punch-in on “When I met him”. There is no Thu Ta footage in this shoot. If Nick gets a real Thu Ta photo or clip from Watsi (Watsi posted a Thu Ta reel on Instagram), use it for 3 s here. Otherwise stay on her.
rows.motion: Captions only. Spell it Thu Ta. The transcript says “Tuta”: that is wrong.

voice.quote: There's a Watsi patient named Thu Ta that I met, and honestly so many others. Our community came together to fund the heart surgery he needed. When I met him, he crossed the border in a river from Myanmar to Thailand to get care, and today he's helping bring health care back to the people in Myanmar who have nowhere else to turn in the middle of a war, and that's what showing up for one person can become.

rows.music: Bed steady. Keep it warm, not dramatic, on “war”.

voice.quote: I used to think scale meant doing things big, but I've come to think it means taking care to do things right, and bringing even more people along with you, building a shared vision, and then doing it again and again until it compounds.

rows.visual: On her. Optional lift if V1 runs long: drop this row first.
rows.motion: Brand touch (the only one): a hand-drawn circle from the September Spirit “Extras” set draws around the caption “35,000” in 8 frames, Watsi cyan #11BAED. Holds 1 s, then off.

voice.quote: One patient in Nepal became 35,000 patients. More than 20 million dollars moved to where it can do the most good. That's what compounding looks like, and it's just the start.

rows.visual: On her. Slow 2% push-in across the line.

voice.quote: I used to think that working in global health was about building the very best systems. I don't really believe that anymore. I think it's so much more about the people. Who you are serving, and who are you accountable to, who's around the table doing the hard work together.

rows.visual: Back to 100%. Hold 1 second on her face after “showing up for”.

voice.quote: That's the most important thing I've learned. People are always worth showing up for.

rows.visual: Clean end card. Light cyan #D3EDFA background. Navy is never a background.
rows.motion: watsi.org, all lowercase, Lato, navy #2E2844. One line. Nothing under it. No stats, no donate button.

tech: 3840×2160, 23.976 fps, H.264, 2-ch audio recorded into the camera
1080×1920 at 23.976 fps. Same as the source. No frame-rate change.
A 9:16 crop of 4K is 1215×2160, so it is sharper than 1080×1920. Punch-ins up to 112% stay native. The room is dim: lift exposure and skin a little, keep it natural.
2 channels recorded into the camera. Pick the live channel on the waveform and map it to both sides. Mute the other. (Not measured: the Drive download limit stopped the audio check.)
Lato Bold, white, soft shadow, large. Pop word by word. No highlight box, no shading block. One line at a time. Always on screen, also in pauses. Keep the bottom 20% clear for app buttons.
Same edit on a 1920×1080 timeline, no crop. Move the top text and supers into the 16:9 safe area.
checklist: Read every caption against the audio. Sonam checks every word, and typos are her top complaint.
The transcript writes “WOTC”. It is Watsi, capital W only. The URL is watsi.org, all lowercase.
The question is on screen from frame 1 and stays at least 5 seconds.
Name super “Mackinnon” is large, first name only, and never at 0:00.
Captions never drop out, even in pauses.
Keep her natural pauses. The delivery must sound like her, not a teleprompter.
Thu Ta is two words. “35,000” and “20 million dollars” match what she says.
Nothing from the first run (00:11–00:58) is in the cut.

decisions.b: Nick's brief asks for 16:9 + 9:16. Watsi ad cuts are one ratio only, but this is not an ad, so the plan follows the brief. Nick: confirm the 16:9 is still wanted, or drop it.

client_note: Why this matters: Sonam wants a real person at the center. Thu Ta is that person. The cut lives or dies on his 20 seconds.
